description: Customer-service platform with Support ticketing for tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.
self_serve_details: Zendesk lists self-serve trials and paid Support/Suite plans. API requests require a verified user; OAuth access is instance-bound, while public multi-customer integrations must use a global OAuth client. The opened pricing page does not map API access to a specific trial or plan, so a free-credential conclusion is not assigned.

credential_access.path: Use a verified Zendesk user and an OAuth client/token for the target instance. Zendesk API tokens can be managed in Admin Center, but the official guide marks them deprecated; multi-customer apps must use a global OAuth token.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Verified user and account authorization are required. Regular instance OAuth is not sufficient for a public multi-customer integration; the developer terms require global OAuth. API tokens are deprecated and use Basic authentication.

api.details: The official Support/Ticketing API covers tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows with standard REST resources. Rate limits and certain advanced entitlements are account/endpoint dependent; this assessment does not infer MCP from the REST API.

mcp.details: No first-party Zendesk MCP server was established in the reviewed material. This is an unresolved field, not a NOT_FOUND claim.
mcp.search_scope: Targeted search of developer.zendesk.com for Zendesk MCP returned no results; opened the official security/auth and Support Ticketing API references. No comprehensive Zendesk-owned repository, marketplace, or all-product documentation audit was performed, so status remains UNKNOWN.

buildability.blocker: Verified account access and OAuth client setup are required; public distribution requires global OAuth. Plan-to-API entitlement and official MCP availability remain unresolved.
buildability.rationale: A broad official REST API supports core support actions, but the required verified-user/OAuth setup and global OAuth rule for multi-customer distribution add material constraints.

evidence.claim: Zendesk positions its product as an AI customer-service platform with ticketing and support plans.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened pricing page describes the customer-service solution and lists Support ticketing and Suite service plans.

evidence.claim: Zendesk API supports OAuth access tokens sent as Bearer tokens; API tokens are a separate deprecated Basic-auth method.
evidence.source_title: Security and authentication | Zendesk Developer Docs
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official page documents OAuth Bearer requests and API-token Basic auth, and labels API tokens deprecated.

evidence.claim: API requests require a verified Zendesk user; OAuth tokens address one instance and public integrations must use global OAuth tokens.
evidence.source_title: Security and authentication | Zendesk Developer Docs
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The page says a verified user is required, instance OAuth is tied to the client instance, and public multi-customer apps must use global OAuth.

evidence.claim: Zendesk offers trial signup and paid Support/Suite plans, but the opened pricing page does not establish which plan confers API access.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened page lists Try for free, Support Team and Suite plans; no API entitlement-to-plan mapping was established.

evidence.claim: Zendesk's Support API is the Ticketing API for tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official Ticketing introduction names tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflow management.

evidence.claim: The opened official Zendesk API references describe REST/auth but do not establish an official MCP server; status is kept UNKNOWN.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: This page is an API reference and does not itself make an MCP ownership or availability claim.

evidence.claim: Zendesk REST is buildable for core support actions, subject to verified-user auth and global OAuth for public distribution.
evidence.source_title: Security and authentication | Zendesk Developer Docs
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official auth docs distinguish instance OAuth from the required global OAuth approach for apps distributed to multiple customers.

limitations: No Zendesk instance, verified account, OAuth client, API call, or plan entitlement was tested.
The pricing page does not map API access to a trial or tier.
MCP status remains UNKNOWN after a bounded official-domain search; no broad repository/marketplace audit was completed.
researcher_notes: API tokens are documented but deprecated; do not treat public API documentation or a free trial as proof of unrestricted production credentials.

description: Customer-service platform for support conversations, messaging, shared inboxes, tickets, and customer data, with Fin AI features.
self_serve_details: Intercom offers self-serve trial signup, but the official Conversations API reference says the API is available only to apps with a trial or active subscription. Plan, usage, and API scope conditions still apply; the pricing page does not state trial duration in the opened text.

credential_access.path: For a private integration, create an app in the target workspace and retrieve its access token in Developer Hub. For an app accessing other workspaces, implement OAuth; Intercom says not to request customers' private access tokens.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Conversations API requires a trial or active subscription. OAuth is required for public/multi-workspace apps, and tokens/scopes inherit workspace permissions. Official MCP supports US and EU hosted workspaces, not AU.

api.details: Directly reviewed REST documentation covers conversation creation, listing, replying, and management; the first-party MCP guide additionally documents access to conversations, contacts, companies, articles, and other API-backed tools. The REST endpoint inventory was not exhaustively sampled in this batch, so breadth is conservatively MODERATE.

mcp.details: Intercom hosts official remote MCP endpoints: https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp for US and https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp for EU workspaces. Official docs list 14 tools; user permissions and requested OAuth/API permissions govern access. AU-hosted workspaces are not yet supported.
mcp.search_scope: Opened first-party Intercom/Fin MCP guide, API authentication docs, and the Conversations API reference. MCP availability and regional restriction are explicit; no MCP session was connected or tested.

buildability.blocker: A workspace trial or active subscription is needed for the Conversations API; public apps use OAuth, and MCP is unavailable for AU-hosted workspaces.
buildability.rationale: Documented REST operations and an official MCP provide useful agent access, but subscription, OAuth consent/scope, and workspace-region requirements affect rollout.

description: Customer-support helpdesk for ticketing, shared inboxes, customer portals, knowledge bases, and agent workflows.
self_serve_details: The current Freshdesk support plan matrix marks API-key functionality unavailable on Free and available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise. Pricing offers self-serve trial entry for paid plans, but trial entitlements were not tested. Freshdesk MCP is generally available on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise with plan-based action allowances and optional action packs.

credential_access.path: A verified agent retrieves the personal API key from Profile Settings after CAPTCHA verification. API calls use the key with HTTP Basic authentication; the agent's role permissions govern permitted actions.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: The current plan table excludes Free from API-key/API functionality. MCP supports Growth, Pro, and Enterprise only, with per-minute limits and annual included actions; the published Freshdesk pricing page lists additional MCP action packs.

api.details: The official REST v2 reference documents ticket CRUD, conversations/replies, contacts, companies, agents, ticket fields/forms, and other helpdesk resources. API quotas are plan-based. The separate official MCP surface is an API-key-authenticated agent interface, not a separate REST API type.

mcp.details: Freshworks' first-party Freshdesk MCP endpoint is https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp. Freshdesk support says GA began September 10, 2026, supports MCP-compatible clients, and currently authenticates with an API key only. Growth, Pro, and Enterprise have annual included action allowances and per-minute limits.
mcp.search_scope: Opened Freshdesk API reference, first-party MCP support article, current API-key help article, and Freshdesk pricing page. MCP plan matrix and API-key plan matrix are directly documented; no MCP connection was tested.

buildability.blocker: Free excludes API access; verified API-key/role access, paid-tier rate limits, and the Freshdesk MCP action allowance/add-on structure constrain deployment.
buildability.rationale: Freshdesk offers broad REST resources and a first-party MCP integration, but a supported paid plan, verified agent credentials, and usage quotas are material requirements.

description: Customer-operations platform with a shared inbox and APIs for syncing, retrieving, creating, updating, and deleting conversations and related resources.
self_serve_details: Front provides a free developer environment for API work, limited to three teammates. API tokens are a quick path for an internal/single-customer integration; public integrations must use OAuth unless Front grants an exception. Public partnership/listing is a separate process.

credential_access.path: Create a free Front developer account and generate an API token for internal or single-customer testing; register a developer app/OAuth feature for a public integration. The MCP server also requires a confidential OAuth connection carrying client ID and secret.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Public distribution requires OAuth unless Front grants an exception. Front MCP is open beta, does not support Dynamic Client Registration, and inherits the authorizing teammate's permissions and selected scopes.

api.details: The Core API supports CRUD across contacts, comments, tags, conversations and other entities; webhooks support real-time events. Front also documents separate Channel API, Plugin SDK, and connector surfaces, which are not counted as Core REST endpoints here.

mcp.details: Front operates an official open-beta remote MCP server at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp. It uses OAuth 2.1/PKCE-compatible confidential client credentials, per-user authorization, and read/write/send scopes; clients requiring DCR cannot connect.
mcp.search_scope: Opened Front's first-party Welcome, Authentication, and MCP Server pages. The dev-account and API framework are explicit; open-beta status, endpoint, auth, and DCR limitation are explicit.

buildability.blocker: Public integrations require OAuth; Front MCP is open beta and requires a client ID/secret (no DCR). Tools inherit the user's role and scopes.
buildability.rationale: A free developer environment and broad REST/webhook surfaces enable development, but public distribution, beta MCP compatibility, OAuth setup, and user-scoped authorization are material constraints.

evidence.claim: Front describes its platform APIs as covering shared-inbox data and operations including contacts, comments, tags, syncing, and conversation actions.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened overview lists Core API CRUD, MCP, Connectors, Plugin SDK, Channel API, and Chat Widget.

evidence.claim: Front Core API accepts Bearer tokens obtained through settings API tokens or OAuth; public integrations must use OAuth absent an exception.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official guide documents Bearer token requests, internal token use, OAuth, and the public-integration OAuth rule.

evidence.claim: Front offers a free developer environment limited to three teammates and documents API-token creation for internal work and app OAuth credentials for public work.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official welcome page provides a free developer signup path, a three-teammate limit, and links to create/manage apps.

evidence.claim: Front public integrations use the app framework and OAuth; a developer account is self-serve and free for development.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: First-party partnership page says developers can sign up for a free development account and distinguish public partnership from a private/single-client integration.

evidence.claim: Front's Core API supports CRUD across Front entities and webhooks for real-time changes.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened API overview names contacts, comments, tags, and Core API read/create/update/delete plus webhooks.

evidence.claim: Front hosts an open-beta MCP server at mcp.frontapp.com/mcp with OAuth 2.1/PKCE-compatible confidential credentials, per-user scopes, and no DCR support.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official MCP guide states endpoint, open beta, transport, client-secret requirement, per-user identity, scopes, and DCR incompatibility.

evidence.claim: Front APIs are buildable with an internal token or public OAuth app, while public distribution and MCP client compatibility add constraints.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The official guide makes OAuth mandatory for public integrations unless an exception is granted; MCP needs a confidential OAuth connection.

limitations: No Front account, OAuth app, API token, API call, or MCP session was created.
MCP is explicitly open beta; tool behavior and client compatibility may change.
Front's current product-specific subscription/API entitlement was not tested; the documented free development environment is not equated with production access.
researcher_notes: Do not confuse the free developer sandbox/environment with an entitled production customer account. MCP permission scope is per authorizing teammate.

description: B2B customer-support platform with programmatic access to customer accounts, issues, contacts, messages, and related support data.
self_serve_details: Official API and support docs establish API/MCP credentials inside an existing Pylon workspace, but the reviewed pricing URL repeatedly redirected to a demo-booking page. A public signup/trial path and the precise plan entitlement for API/MCP therefore remain unresolved.

credential_access.path: For REST API access, an Admin creates a named token in Settings > API Tokens; the token is shown once and sent as Authorization: Bearer. For MCP, a Member or Admin seat authorizes through browser OAuth; Viewer and Integration seats cannot connect.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: API-token creation is admin-only. MCP is OAuth-only (no API key or machine-to-machine authentication), requires a Member/Admin seat, and inherits the user's Pylon permissions. The specific plan gate could not be verified from an opened pricing matrix.

api.details: Pylon's first-party API/Webhooks material says integrations can read and act on data across accounts, contacts, issues, messages, tasks/projects, knowledge base, custom fields/objects, tags, macros, surveys, teams, and users; webhooks push events to customer endpoints.

mcp.details: Pylon's official MCP endpoint is https://mcp.usepylon.com/. It uses browser OAuth only, acts on behalf of the logged-in user, and supports issue/account/contact access; notebook block content is not currently retrievable through MCP.
mcp.search_scope: Opened Pylon's API index/authentication docs, API & Webhooks page, and Pylon support articles on API tokens and MCP. Pricing URL attempts redirected to the general demo form, so account/plan access was not resolved.

buildability.blocker: REST tokens require a Pylon Admin; MCP requires a Member/Admin OAuth login and cannot use machine credentials. Account/trial/plan entitlement remains unknown.
buildability.rationale: A broad documented REST/webhook surface and official hosted MCP make the connector technically feasible, but credentials are role-gated, MCP is OAuth-only, and pricing/account access was not established.

evidence.claim: Pylon describes its API as programmatic access to Pylon data and its MCP as a way for AI tools to access support issues, accounts, and contacts.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official API overview names customer and issue data and directs users to the complete endpoint reference.

evidence.claim: Pylon REST requests use a Bearer API token; Pylon MCP uses a separate browser OAuth flow.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official API docs specify Authorization: Bearer; Pylon's MCP setup article explicitly requires OAuth and says API-key auth is unavailable for MCP.

evidence.claim: Only Admin users can create API tokens from Settings > API Tokens; a token is shown once and can be role-limited.
evidence.source_title: How do I create a Pylon API token? | Pylon Knowledge Base
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened support article documents the settings path, one-time token display, and admin/permission requirement.

evidence.claim: The attempted official Pylon pricing URLs redirected to a demo-booking page rather than an inspectable plan matrix, so self-serve/trial and plan entitlement remain unknown.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Direct fetch returned a required-field 30-minute demo form; it did not expose pricing or API/MCP plan availability.

evidence.claim: Pylon documents REST API and webhooks for reading and acting on multiple support object groups, including customers/accounts, issues, messages, tasks/projects, knowledge base, and custom objects.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened first-party integration page describes API reads/writes and event webhooks across the named resource areas.

evidence.claim: Pylon hosts an OAuth-only MCP server at mcp.usepylon.com; it requires a Member/Admin seat and inherits the authorizing user's permissions.
evidence.source_title: How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server? | Pylon Knowledge Base
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official support article gives endpoint, OAuth-only rule, no machine/API-key auth, user-scoped access, and Member/Admin seat requirement.

evidence.claim: Pylon can be integrated through REST/webhooks or official MCP, but API token creation is Admin-only and MCP requires interactive OAuth and an eligible seat.
evidence.source_title: How do I connect to the Pylon MCP Server? | Pylon Knowledge Base
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official setup guide distinguishes OAuth MCP from REST Bearer token authentication and documents eligible seat types.

limitations: No Pylon workspace, API token, trial, MCP session, or account signup was used.
Pricing/trial/API-plan status is unresolved: three official pricing URL attempts resolved to a demo page; search snippets were treated only as discovery and not as evidence.
Pylon MCP does not currently expose notebook block content; OAuth sessions expire and may require reconnection.
researcher_notes: Do not transfer the REST API's admin-created Bearer token model to MCP; MCP is OAuth-only. The pricing redirect is preserved as a research limitation rather than filled from search snippets.

description: Helpdesk and customer-support suite with ticketing, live chat, knowledge base, automation, and call-center features.
self_serve_details: LiveAgent advertises a 30-day no-credit-card trial and paid per-agent tiers. Its hosted MCP tools count against the account's AI-credit budget; the current API v3 reference is available from within a customer account, so the trial does not by itself prove every API operation or entitlement.

credential_access.path: For MCP, an agent generates an access token from Profile > MCP Integration or completes OAuth 2.1 authorization-code/PKCE. The legacy public REST API reference uses an API key; the API v3 reference is exposed inside the LiveAgent account.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: MCP actions run under the connecting agent's role permissions and consume the account's AI-credit budget. The public API v1 material is older; full API v3 documentation/testing requires an account session.

api.details: The opened public REST API v1 reference documents conversations/messages, customers, companies, knowledge-base articles, reports, tags, files, and agents. LiveAgent also says API v3 documentation and interactive testing are available inside the account; v3 endpoint details were not inspected here.

mcp.details: LiveAgent offers a tenant-specific hosted MCP server at https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp with Streamable HTTP and either generated Bearer tokens or OAuth 2.1 authorization-code + PKCE. Tools execute as the agent and are limited by their role; MCP calls count against AI credits.
mcp.search_scope: Opened LiveAgent's first-party MCP article, public API v1 reference, and pricing page. The MCP guide is current; the REST v1 reference is older and current API v3 docs require account access.

buildability.blocker: The server URL is tenant-specific, agent role permissions apply, MCP uses AI credits, and the current v3 API reference is account-gated.
buildability.rationale: A broad REST surface and first-party MCP are documented, but tenant-specific setup, role-scoped actions, credit consumption, and limited public visibility into current API v3 details affect implementation.

evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened pricing page lists ticketing, chat, knowledge base, customer portal, automation, and call-center features.

evidence.claim: LiveAgent's public REST v1 reference accepts an API key parameter; the separate MCP server supports generated Bearer access tokens or OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: MCP article documents the hosted URL, Bearer token and OAuth 2.1 flows; the public API reference shows an API key parameter.

evidence.claim: An agent can generate an MCP token in Profile > MCP Integration or authorize an OAuth client; actions are attributed to the agent identity.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The setup page describes profile token creation, OAuth approval, revocation, and actor attribution.

evidence.claim: LiveAgent offers a 30-day free trial without a credit card and lists paid Small/Medium/Large/Enterprise tiers.

evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened plan comparison states 30 days free trial, no credit card required, and per-agent paid tiers.

evidence.claim: LiveAgent's public REST v1 reference covers conversations/messages, customers, companies, knowledge base, reports, tags, files, and agents.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened API reference table of contents lists the named resource groups and read/write operations.

evidence.claim: LiveAgent's first-party MCP endpoint is tenant-specific and uses Streamable HTTP with Bearer token or OAuth 2.1/PKCE; tools run under agent permissions and consume AI credits.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The support article documents endpoint/auth modes, full tool access subject to role, audit attribution, and AI-credit budget impact.

evidence.claim: LiveAgent supports REST and first-party MCP but deployment depends on an existing tenant, agent permissions, AI-credit budget, and tenant-specific endpoint.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official guide specifies user identity, role-based permissions, per-tenant URL, and credit consumption.

limitations: No LiveAgent account, API key, MCP token, OAuth client, or API call was used.
The public API v1 page is legacy; the API v3 reference is exposed within an account and was not inspected.

description: Support platform for customer-service teams with thread, customer, tenant, and workflow data exposed through GraphQL and agent tooling.
self_serve_details: Plain advertises a seven-day free trial with no credit card and self-serve Foundation pricing. API credentials require a workspace machine user and explicitly selected permissions; the opened pricing table does not reliably map every API/MCP capability to each tier.

credential_access.path: In a Plain workspace, create a Machine User under Settings > Machine Users, add a fine-grained API key, and copy it once. For hosted MCP, connect by OAuth; the MCP inherits the user's permissions and requires openid and offline_access scopes.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Machine-user key permissions are explicit and granular. The MCP is user-scoped and write actions may require client confirmation; API feature availability by plan was not fully mapped in the pricing extraction.

api.details: Plain's GraphQL API is the same API used by the product and its documentation says it has no UI/API capability gap. The docs provide customer/thread operations and a schema/typed SDK; breadth is judged broad for the documented support data model, not by endpoint count.

mcp.details: Plain operates https://mcp.plain.com/mcp with OAuth. The official guide lists 30 read/write tools spanning threads, customers, tenants, and support actions; OAuth inherits the user's access and requires openid offline_access scopes.
mcp.search_scope: Opened Plain GraphQL introduction/authentication, official MCP setup, and pricing pages. An initial noncanonical /docs/api URL returned 404; the current GraphQL docs URL was found and opened. No live workspace/token/MCP session was tested.

buildability.blocker: A workspace and machine-user permission setup are required for API keys; hosted MCP requires interactive OAuth and client support for token refresh/scopes. Plan mapping is incomplete.
buildability.rationale: Plain offers a broad documented GraphQL API and first-party MCP, but credentials are scoped, OAuth is user-bound, and ongoing plan/API entitlement details need confirmation for a production deployment.

evidence.claim: Plain's product documentation describes a support platform whose GraphQL API is used by the product itself and provides access to customer/workflow data.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official API introduction says Plain itself is built on the same GraphQL API and links support-agent operations.

evidence.claim: Plain's GraphQL API uses Bearer authentication with a machine-user API key; the hosted MCP uses OAuth.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The API guide documents machine users, fine-grained API keys, and Authorization: Bearer; the separate MCP guide documents OAuth.

evidence.claim: A workspace user creates a Machine User and a permission-scoped API key in Settings; the key is shown once.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The official guide lists Settings > Machine Users, Add API Key, explicit permission selection, and one-time copy.

evidence.claim: Plain offers a seven-day free trial without a credit card and a self-serve Foundation plan; API feature placement is not fully mapped in the extracted pricing table.
evidence.source_title: Plain Pricing — Plans from $35/seat/month | 7-Day Free Trial
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened pricing page says start today/no credit card, shows Foundation/Horizon/Frontier, and a seven-day trial; extension rows do not reliably map every feature to plan.

evidence.claim: Plain's GraphQL API is used by its own product and the docs describe a schema, customer operations, and a typed SDK.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Official page gives GraphQL endpoint, schema URL, customer query example, and links API schema/SDK documentation.

evidence.claim: Plain hosts an official MCP server at mcp.plain.com/mcp with OAuth, user permission inheritance, and 30 tools including reads and writes.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: Opened guide names endpoint, OAuth, required scopes, inherited permissions, and the tool table across threads/customers/tenants.

evidence.claim: Plain is technically buildable via GraphQL or MCP, but scoped machine-user keys, OAuth client support, and uncertain plan mapping constrain deployment.
evidence.excerpt_or_observation: The guide documents user-scoped OAuth, required scopes, refresh considerations, and client behavior; API docs document scoped machine-user keys.

limitations: No Plain account, machine user, API key, trial, API call, or MCP session was created.
An initial /docs/api URL returned 404; the authoritative current GraphQL docs were found and opened.
